source.title: Why Better Models Can Create Riskier Systems: Evidence from LLM Agents in Financial Markets
source.authors: Jillian Ross; Eric C. So; Zoe De Simone; Charles Pozniak; Andrew W. Lo

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses the Platonic Representation Hypothesis as a possible explanation, but its own experiments measure correlations in trading actions and market outcomes, not representational similarity or convergence.
record.gate_note: The paper reports capability-related correlations in non-corrective trading actions, which are related to—but do not measure—the representational convergence in the claim versions. Its price-discovery and misinformation results concern financial-market outcomes, not representations. No rows are assigned to V1–V7.
record.test_reason: The study measures pairwise correlation of residual trading actions (behaviour), not internal representations. It does not test any version. It cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis only as one possible explanation and leaves the mechanism to future work. The capability–behavioural-correlation result is a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find that more capable LLMs show more correlated non-corrective trading behaviour, that shared accurate signals improve price discovery, and that shared adversarial misinformation makes markets worse than noise-only. They say they 'empirically show this convergence', but this is behavioural convergence; the PRH-like mechanism is explicitly left untested.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce or apply the original representation-similarity methods; it measures correlations in model trading actions.

fits_no_version.finding: Pair-average capability predicts pairwise correlation of non-corrective trading residuals: ELO t=3.94, p=0.001; MMLU-Pro t=4.88, p<0.001. Shared provider is not significant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More capable LLMs show more correlated residual behaviour on a decision task, independent of provider (behavioural, not representational, convergence).

fits_no_version.finding: Correlated residuals leave a variance floor of 0.010 against a single-model variance of 0.021. A bootstrap over ensembles of 2–8 models tracks the floored theoretical curve.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Behavioural correlation among LLM agents produces non-diversifiable aggregate variance.

record.problems: The paper's empirical evidence is from simulated financial markets. The RQ1 correlation analysis uses 7 models and 21 model pairs; it does not measure internal representations. Some ensemble-scaling evidence is reported only through a figure and qualitative description.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were included for RQ2 or RQ3 price-tracking, volatility, or directional-accuracy results: these report financial-market outcomes rather than representational alignment or its direct measurement.

untested.parts: No representational similarity across models or scale is measured; only correlation of trading-action residuals versus capability.
No cross-modal or paired image-caption alignment.
No seed comparison or shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching or relative representations.
No interpretable features or circuits compared.
No comparison of similarity metrics or input distributions.
Representational alignment and its causes are not measured. The shared-provider null concerns behavioural correlation only.

record.verdict_notes: Simulated single-asset market with small model panels (7–8 models in RQ1, 3 in RQ2/RQ3). RQ2/RQ3 rows are correctly left out as market outcomes. The paper also cites a recent challenge to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis (arXiv:2604.18572), which may be relevant for the V2 and V6 search.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not compare internal representations or their similarity across models as model size or capability changes.
No paired image-caption representations or cross-modal alignment are measured.
The study does not compare representations across training seeds or identify shared features or subspaces.
No representation mapping, stitching, relative representation, or unpaired alignment method is tested.
The study does not test whether interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
The study does not compare representational similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions.
The study does not measure representational alignment or test whether shared data or objectives explain such alignment.

rows.subject: 7 LLMs (aggregate panel; model identities not stated for this experiment)
rows.operation_detail: Regressed pairwise correlations of per-model OLS residual actions on pair-average capability, controlling for shared provider.

conditions.value: 64, with varied fundamental gaps, momentum, volatility, and analyst views

rows.measure: Pairwise Pearson correlation of non-corrective action residuals; regression on pair-average ELO controlling for shared provider: t = 3.94, p = 0.001, R2 = 0.475. Shared-provider term: p = 0.39.
rows.value: Average capability significantly predicted pairwise non-corrective correlation; shared provider was not significant.
rows.note: The reported result concerns correlated trading behavior, not representational similarity.
rows.check: Link and state are fine. The subject count is ambiguous: the text says 7 LLMs and 21 pairs, Appendix D lists 8 models, and the bootstrap uses N=2 to 8. Which model was excluded from RQ1 is not stated.

rows.subject: LLM ensemble (aggregate; individual models not specified for this calculation)
rows.operation_detail: Estimated the non-diversifiable variance floor for ensemble-mean residual actions.
rows.measure: Variance floor of ensemble-mean residuals, ρ · σr².
rows.value: 0.010, described as roughly half the single-model variance
rows.note: This is a result about correlated residual actions, not representations.

rows.subject: LLM ensemble (aggregate; individual models not specified for this calculation)
rows.operation_detail: Bootstrapped ensembles by drawing models with replacement and compared residual-variance scaling with the theoretical curve.
rows.measure: Variance of ensemble-mean residual actions as ensemble size changes.
rows.baseline: Idealized independent-model benchmark predicting variance decline as 1/N with no floor
rows.value: Figure only; text says the empirical bootstrap closely tracks the theoretical curve, which has a floor.
rows.note: The paper states the bootstrap tracks the theoretical floor; values for individual ensemble sizes are not given in the text.
